answer.reason: The verses tell two chief things of Simeon as a person: the slaughter at Shechem with Levi, and his being bound by Joseph in Egypt.

clauses.english: with Levi, slew all the males of Shechem to avenge their sister Dinah
clauses.quote: Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

clauses.english: was taken and bound by Joseph in Egypt before his brothers' eyes
clauses.quote: took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

doubts: GEN 49:5-7 (Jacob's words on Simeon and Levi) was left out as a pronouncement, not an event.
Tribal verses (the census, camp, lot, and cities of the tribe of Simeon, and the sealing in Revelation) concern the tribe, not the man, and were left out.
1CH 4:42 concerns later Simeonites, not the patriarch, and was left out.
GEN 43:23 (Simeon brought out to his brothers) was left out so that his captivity stays one event.
